prompt: A company bought a competitor two years ago, expecting $20M a year in cost savings. Savings so far are $8M a year, and the two IT systems still run separately. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: The $20M target was likely unrealistic from the start.
options.feedback: Possible, but it ignores the concrete reason the prompt gives: the two IT systems still run separately.

options.text: The two companies' cultures are probably clashing, slowing the merger.
options.feedback: Nothing points to culture. The prompt points to IT.

options.text: IT is the only problem, so the systems have to be merged at any cost.
options.feedback: This states one cause as certain and commits to unlimited spending before any data.

options.text: The separate IT systems are probably what's blocking the savings.
options.feedback: Right. Running two systems usually means duplicated processes and costs. I'd map the planned savings by source against what has been delivered.

explanation: The data shows $8M of the expected $20M in savings, with the two IT systems still running separately. Likely cause: unmerged IT is blocking much of the savings. To test it, map planned savings by source against what has been delivered. If the IT-dependent savings are on track, the original estimate was probably too high.
